items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: I remember John Fell, who was the clarinet player in our band

ctx.x: They were disbanding the Army, get rid of them, get rid of them, and send everybody home. So people were getting out and I remember John Fell, who was the clarinet player in our band, John was in a situation like this, he’d only been in for a while but he was a very bright guy and he could type and — which was not so usual in those days — and he was a clerk somewhere in the Army, and the order came through that if you could go back to college immediately you could be discharged. So he pulled out a form and typed…
They called that the “crazy mixed up years” didn’t they?
